Find the area ${A}_{\text{max}}$ of the largest rectangle that can be inscribed in the closed region bounded by the $x$-axis, the $y$-axis, and the graph of $y=4-2x.$ Do not round the answer.

${A}_{\text{max}}=$
 {{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Let $x$ and $y$ be the width and height of the rectangle, respectively. Given a width $x,$ the height $y$ of the rectangle rises up to the curve $y=4-2x.$

We want to maximize the area of the rectangle, which is given by

$$
A=xy=x(4-2x)=4x-2{x}^{2}.
$$

Let's compute the critical points. Taking the derivative of the area, we get

$$
{A}^{′}(x)=4-4x,
$$

and solving ${A}^{′}(x)=0$ gives the following critical point:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{′}(x) & =0 \\ 4-4x & =0 \\ 4x & =4 \\ x & =1\end{aligned}
$$

All that's left now is to confirm that $x=1$ does indeed give a maximum value of $A(x).$ To do this, we use the first derivative test. We write up a table of values:

| Interval | $(0,1)$ | $1$ | $(1,2)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Test Point | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $$ | $\frac{3}{2}$ |
| ${A}^{′}$ | $+$ | $0$ | $-$ |
| $A$ | $↗$ | $\text{max}$ | $↘$ |

So, $x=1$ does indeed give a maximum, and the area of the resulting rectangle will be the largest possible.

Therefore, the greatest area ${A}_{\text{max}}$ that a rectangle can have is

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{\text{max}}=A(1) & =4(1)-2(1)^{2} \\  & =4-2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
